gloss: view of life and death; philosophy on mortality

definitions.gloss: view of life and death; attitude toward life and death; philosophy on mortality
definitions.explanation: One's personal or cultural perspective on the meaning of life and death, including how one faces mortality and what significance one assigns to living and dying.

examples.japanese: {死生観|しせいかん}は{人|ひと}それぞれだ。
examples.english: Everyone has their own view of life and death.

examples.japanese: {病気|びょうき}を{経験|けいけん}して{死生観|しせいかん}が{変|か}わった。
examples.english: My view of life and death changed after experiencing illness.

examples.japanese: {武士道|ぶしどう}には{独自|どくじ}の{死生観|しせいかん}があり、{死|し}を{恐|おそ}れず{生|い}きることが{美徳|びとく}とされた。
examples.english: Bushido had its own philosophy on life and death, in which living without fear of death was considered a virtue.

notes:
A compound of {死生|しせい} (life and death) and {観|かん} (view, perspective). This is a culturally significant concept in Japanese thought, deeply influenced by Buddhism, Shinto, and the samurai tradition. Discussions of {死生観|しせいかん} are common in literature, philosophy, religion, and end-of-life care contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {死生観|しせいかん}が{変|か}わる: one's view of life and death changes
- {死生観|しせいかん}を{持|も}つ: to hold a view of life and death
- {日本人|にほんじん}の{死生観|しせいかん}: the Japanese view of life and death
- {死生観|しせいかん}に{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}える: to influence one's view on mortality

RELATED TERMS:
- {人生観|じんせいかん}: view of life — focuses only on how one views living, not death
- {世界観|せかいかん}: worldview — broader philosophical outlook on the world
- {価値観|かちかん}: values, sense of values — one's personal value system

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the concept of {死生観|しせいかん} often comes up in discussions about {終活|しゅうかつ} (end-of-life preparation), {看取|みと}り (attending a dying person), and traditional arts like {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony), which incorporate awareness of impermanence ({無常|むじょう}).
